svg.title: PostgreSQL 8 KiB Page Layout, Binary COPY Ingest and Cut-Through Streaming Read Path
svg.desc: Animated diagram showing how pgvs3 stores inline small objects in objects.inline_data and splits larger objects into 8,120-byte chunks that fit exactly one 8,192-byte PostgreSQL page without TOAST, ingested via 4 MiB binary COPY batches and read via parallel REPEATABLE READ bitmap heap scans.
svg.text: 8,120-Byte Page-Aligned Storage Layout & Cut-Through I/O Pipeline
Zero TOAST pointer chasing · O(1) byte-range offset seeking (offset = no × 8,120) · Split B-tree and Bitmap-Scan pools
1. Write & Atomic Publish Pipeline
Fast Path A: Inline Small Objects
• ≤64 KiB (s3b_/s3w_) or ≤8,120 B (s3c_/RESP)
• Stored in objects.inline_data (file_id = NULL)
1 SQL round-trip · 64 KiB pooled buffer
Fast Path B: Streaming Binary COPY (>64 KiB)
1. Allocate immutable file_id from s3p.file_ids
2. Slice stream into 8,120 B blocks (no = 0,1,2…)
3. Compress block with Zstd ONLY if it shrinks
4. Frame 4 MiB binary COPY batches + hash MD5/CRC
Zero temp table · Direct heap page write
Atomic Pointer Swap (publish_object)
• Evaluates If-Match / If-None-Match in same Tx
• PG 18 RETURNING old.file_id, old.parts
• Queues replaced file_id to schema.garbage
• Aborted upload rolls back cleanly; no torn read
Zero-Copy CopyObject & Multipart Assembly
Bounded Reaper & Aggressive Autovacuum
• Retired file_ids kept for --reap-grace (10m)
• Leader deletes 65,536 rows (~508 MiB)/pass
• autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.01
Freed 8 KiB pages recycled in steady state
2. Inside One 8,192-Byte PostgreSQL Page
Table: s3b_<bucket>.chunks (unpartitioned up to 32 TiB)
PostgreSQL 8,192 B Heap Page (BLCKSZ = 8192)
24 B PageHeaderData + 4 B Line Pointer (ItemId)
23 B HeapTupleHeader + Alignment + PK Columns
file_id: INT8 (8 B) · no: INT4 (4 B) · varlena hdr (4 B)
data: BYTEA (up to 8,120 Bytes)
• Compressed Zstd frame if len(zstd) < wantLen
• Raw bytes if len(raw) == wantLen (Parquet)
Never expands incompressible data past 8,120 B!
toast_tuple_target = 8160 · STORAGE EXTERNAL
Why 8,120 Bytes Beats TOAST & Large Objects
• Standard PG TOAST splits at ~2 KiB into a side
table, adding extra index lookups on every read.
• Fixed 8,120 B logical blocks map any HTTP
Range: bytes=A-B directly to chunk numbers:
start_no = A / 8120, end_no = B / 8120
WHERE file_id = $1 AND no BETWEEN $2 AND $3
3. Split-Pool & Cut-Through Read Path
mainPool (enable_indexscan = on)
• Point PK lookup on objects (key, version, ETag)
• Returns inline_data immediately if file_id IS NULL
• Warm cache GET reuses metadata row (1 lookup)
chunkPool (enable_indexscan = off)
• Forces PG 18 Bitmap Heap Scan on chunks
• effective_io_concurrency = 32 (AIO prefetch)
• ≤64 MiB span: 1 range query on chunkPool
• >64 MiB / Multipart: 2–8 parallel 8 MiB pieces
Shared pg_export_snapshot() REPEATABLE READ
TID Reorder + 32-Buffer Cut-Through Ring
• Bitmap scan yields pages in physical TID order;
streamRows reorders in RAM to strict `no` order
• >8 MiB reads feed 32 × 256 KiB channel buffers
• Overlaps DB prefetch with socket Body.WriteTo
Client Memory & Backpressure Safety
• Slow HTTP readers backpressure the 32-slot ring
• Gateway never buffers whole 1 GiB object in RAM
DuckDB 2.0 Async Range Reads Hit O(1) Offsets
